digest.component_or_area: completion verifier resumption mechanism (experimental search-frontier exclusion)
propositions: Experiment tested whether providing prior-attempt search frontier as an exclusion list within ticket context reduces re-search overlap and steps-to-verdict during verifier resumption.

Frontier exclusion block (data-shaped, <=1500 chars) was spliced into untrusted_ticket_context fence during resume attempts via STEP_REGISTRY precheck wrapper, but the fence renders such blocks inert by design.
On both corpus tickets (45c1 and 8d74), treatment arm B showed increased overlap relative to control arm A: 45c1 +78%, 8d74 +60%, both exceeding the 30% reduction threshold required for GO decision.
Frontier block paradoxically acted as a signpost, causing the model to immediately re-read files and re-execute searches listed as already-searched, raising measured tool-call repetition rates.

Cache-seeded resumption (locust behavior) already eliminates dominant redundancy by skipping re-verification of credited criteria; remaining re-grounding of unproven criteria cannot be suppressed by untrusted data blocks.

Production telemetry would require argument-level tool-call transcripts per verifier run (tool name, full arguments, result classification, criterion boundaries), currently not carried in usage_log or verdict cache.
